results.Proposed_Explanation: 247 CMR 9.04(10) supplies the counting convention in terms: 'In order to determine whether a prescription is within date, a pharmacist shall count the day after the prescription was written as day one.' With 1 March as the date written, day one is 2 March and the thirtieth day is 31 March, so 31 March is the last day within date. A counts the date of issue as day one, which the regulation excludes; C and D adopt conventions the regulation does not use; and E fails because 9.04(10) is a general convention that does not vary by schedule, the schedule fixing only the length of the window (compare M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(a) for Schedule II and 247 CMR 9.04(12) and (13) for Schedules VI and V). Key B confirmed. Auditor disclosure: my Phase-1 blind answer was A. I had located and read 247 CMR 9.04(1) to (9) but not 9.04(10), and in its absence I reasoned from the statutory phrase 'shall become invalid 30 days after the date of issuance' in s. 23(a) and recorded an express reservation that no Massachusetts provision I had retrieved fixed the counting convention. 247 CMR 9.04(10) does fix it, and it fixes it against my blind answer. The author's key is right and my blind answer was wrong.
